headline: NFL Munich Final: Lions dominate Patriots 35-10 behind Gibbs' 252 yards; Maye hurt
teaser: Jahmyr Gibbs explodes for 252 scrimmage yards with two touchdowns and Amon-Ra St. Brown catches two scores in front of 70,225 at Allianz Arena, while Patriots quarterback Drake Maye exits early with an ankle injury.
story:
The Detroit Lions delivered a commanding performance on European soil on Sunday, 15 November, dismantling the New England Patriots 35-10 in the NFL Week 10 international fixture at Allianz Arena in Munich.

Dan Campbell's high-powered attack overwhelmed New England from the opening snap. Jared Goff orchestrated a masterclass, completing 22 of 28 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns. Wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother is German, ignited the raucous crowd of 70,225 with a 56-yard touchdown catch on Detroit's first possession and added a second score in the third quarter.

Running back Jahmyr Gibbs put on a breathtaking show, totaling 252 scrimmage yards (153 rushing, 99 receiving) and scoring twice, including a dazzling 44-yard breakaway touchdown in the fourth quarter. The Patriots' afternoon unraveled early when rookie starter Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury during an Aidan Hutchinson sack on the opening drive and was ruled out, leaving backup Tommy DeVito under constant siege. The victory lifts Detroit to 7-2, while New England drops to 5-5.
whyCareReason: Detroit solidifies NFC contender status with a 35-10 European showcase blowout as Jahmyr Gibbs posts a franchise-record international yardage display.
stakes: Detroit (7-2) tightens its grip on the NFC North race while New England (5-5) deals with quarterback uncertainty following Drake Maye's ankle injury.
rivalryAngle: Electric Munich atmosphere at Allianz Arena as 70,225 German fans witness Dan Campbell's Lions dominate in the final international regular-season clash of 2026.
funFacts: Jahmyr Gibbs generated 252 total scrimmage yards (153 rushing, 99 receiving) with two touchdowns.
Amon-Ra St. Brown caught two touchdowns in Munich in front of his German-born family.
Aidan Hutchinson logged his ninth sack of the season, forcing Drake Maye out of the contest.
